newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African money shortage jumps to over 10 bln rand.
newsitem.headline: S.African money shortage jumps to over 10 bln rand.

text.p: South Africa's money market shortage jumped to 10.608 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.475 billion on Saturday, the Reserve Bank said.

Tuesday's money market shortage - the amount of money the central band lends to commercial banks for their day-to-day operations - was the highest since the record 10.955 billion recorded on April 30 this year, a Reserve Bank spokesman said.
South African short-term interest rates are trading at their highest level this year, after kicking up last week as the annual year-end liquidity squeeze bit deeper.
The squeeze occurs each year in the run-up to Christmas as annual bonuses are paid out, consumers draw large amounts of money, and notes and coins in circulation in the money market system increase.
Major banks on Wednesday quoted three-month NCD rates unchanged at between 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also steady at 16.70 to 17.00 percent.
